title: Goldman Sachs sees S&P 500 at 8,700 despite rare Shiller PE warning
key_facts: Goldman Sachs Research forecasts S&P 500 at 8,700 in 12 months, about 13.5% above the 2 Oct close
S&P 500 earnings per share grew 51% in Q2 from a year earlier and 26% over four quarters, versus a 30-year average of 7%
Almost half of this year's EPS growth comes from AI investment
Forward P/E has fallen from 23 a year ago to 19, matching its 10-year average; Shiller PE (CAPE) is above 40, seen only at the dot-com peak and now
Goldman expects EPS growth of about 11% in 2027 and 2028 ($415 and $460)
Largest US hyperscalers on track for $800 billion capex this year, 94% more than 2025; Goldman analysts expect $1.2 trillion in 2027 and $1.4 trillion in 2028
AI investment expected to turn into a marginal drag on earnings growth in 2028
quote_evidence: "Because equity prices have failed to keep pace with surging earnings, near-term valuations show no hint of a bubble," Snider writes.
"Even an 'average' multiple may be expensive if current earnings are unsustainable," acknowledges Snider.
why_it_matters_hint: The forecast rests on profit growth continuing after the AI spending boost fades.
notes: Older news: the Goldman report was first released 21 Sep 2026 (S&P 500 at 7,764 then); Financial Express re-reports it with the 2 Oct close of 7,666.45 against a record 7,816.70. Article carries a no-advice disclaimer.
